title: Analytic pipelines to assess immune response and germline genetics in human tumors
author: Sayaman, Saad, et al.

steps.title: Prepare immune trait file
steps.instruction: Download the formatted immune‑trait input file “Immune.pheno.139.source.coded.TCGAID.9769.txt” from the Sayaman et al. 2021 GitHub repository.

steps.title: Create ancestry sample lists
steps.instruction: Obtain ancestry assignments (Table S1) and the four ancestry‑specific TCGA ID files (“TCGAID_Cluster1.EUR.8036.txt”, “TCGAID_Cluster2.ASIAN.605.txt”, “TCGAID_Cluster3.AFR.904.txt”, “TCGAID_Cluster4.AMR.222.txt”) from the same GitHub repository.

steps.title: Subset individuals per ancestry
steps.instruction: For each ancestry cluster, run PLINK to keep only the listed TCGA IDs:

substeps.instruction: plink --bfile [input_file] --keep [ancestry_cluster_sample_file_list] --make-bed --out [output_filename]

steps.title: Estimate ancestry‑specific GRM
steps.instruction: Using GCTA, create a genetic relatedness matrix (GRM) from all autosomal SNPs with minor‑allele frequency > 0.01 for each ancestry group.

substeps.instruction: gcta64 --bfile [input_filename] --autosome --maf 0.01 --make-grm --out [output_filename] --thread-num [numeric_value_number_threads]

steps.title: Filter related individuals
steps.instruction: Remove one individual from each pair with estimated relatedness > 0.05.

substeps.instruction: gcta64 --grm [input_filename] --grm-cutoff 0.05 --make-grm --out [output_filename]

steps.title: Run GCTA GREML unconstrained
steps.instruction: Estimate SNP‑heritability for each immune trait using the GREML algorithm without constraints, including categorical covariates, continuous covariates, and the appropriate number of threads.

substeps.instruction: gcta64 --reml-no-constrain --grm [input_filename] --pheno [immune_trait_matrix_filename] --mpheno [immune_trait_numeric_index_input_matrix] --covar [categorical_covariates_filename] --qcovar [continuous_covariates_filename] --thread-num [numeric_value_number_threads] --out [output_filename]

steps.title: Extract heritability estimates
steps.instruction: From each GCTA “.hsq” result file, record the Vg/Vp estimate, its standard error, the likelihood‑ratio test (LRT) p‑value, and the sample size (n) for the corresponding immune trait.

steps.title: Concatenate and annotate results
steps.instruction: Combine the per‑trait .hsq files into a single table and annotate each row with the immune‑trait name, immune category, and immune module (Table S2).

substeps.instruction: Append annotated result files from all traits into one master file.

steps.title: Adjust for multiple testing
steps.instruction: Apply the Benjamini‑Hochberg procedure to the concatenated table to compute FDR‑adjusted p‑values for each ancestry group.

steps.title: Optional heritability visualization
steps.instruction: Plot % heritability (Vg/Vp × 100) across all traits for each ancestry group for exploratory analysis.

steps.title: Create GRanges from GWAS SNPs
steps.instruction: Import the GWAS suggestive and genome‑wide significant SNP table into R, build a data frame of SNP ID, chromosome, and base‑pair position, and convert it to a GRanges object with makeGRangesFromDataFrame.

steps.title: Overlap SNPs with Roadmap epigenomes
steps.instruction: For each Roadmap Epigenomics Project 18‑state BED file, import with rtracklayer and extract the epigenomic state overlapping each SNP GRanges entry using mergeByOverlaps.

substeps.instruction: Import BED: rtracklayer::import("<epigenome>.bed")
Extract state: mergeByOverlaps(snpGR, epigenomeGR)

steps.title: Map epigenome IDs to descriptions
steps.instruction: Join the extracted epigenome IDs to source‑cell‑type and tissue‑type descriptions using the file “Roadmap.metadata.qc.jul2013.csv”.

steps.title: Annotate epigenomic states with colors
steps.instruction: Add color information to each epigenomic state using the “FigureColors.csv” file.

steps.title: Curate immune‑associated epigenomes
steps.instruction: Manually retain epigenomes relevant to immune biology based on cell‑type or tissue of origin (see Table S4).

steps.title: Download TCGA expression matrix
steps.instruction: Retrieve “EBPlusPlusAdjustPANCAN_IlluminaHiSeq_RNASeqV2.geneExp.tsv” from the GDC Pan‑Cancer Atlas portal.

steps.title: Obtain gene annotation
steps.instruction: Using the biomaRt R package, download gene chromosome, start, end, and type (protein‑coding, pseudogene, miRNA, etc.) from Ensembl GRCh37; keep columns “Chromosome”, “Start”, “End”, and “Gene type”.

steps.title: Transpose expression matrix
steps.instruction: Run the R script “OrganizeRNAMatrix.R” to transpose the gene‑expression matrix.

steps.title: Run TCGA eQTL analysis
steps.instruction: Associate genome‑wide and suggestive SNPs with genes within ±1 Mb using linear regression that adjusts for ancestry PCs 1‑7, sex, age, and cancer type (script “eQTLanalysis.R”). The script also performs cancer‑type‑specific eQTLs for the 30 cancers.

steps.title: Summarize eQTL output
steps.instruction: Create a table containing chromosome, position, gene name, distance to gene, pan‑cancer sample size, effect size, p‑value, and the same fields for each individual cancer type.

steps.title: Download GTEx splicing data
steps.instruction: Obtain 5′, 3′, exon‑skipping, intron‑retention, and mutually exclusive exon splice‑event files from the GDC Pan‑Cancer Atlas Splicing 2018 release.

steps.title: Prepare GTEx splicing inputs
steps.instruction: Run “PrepareData.sh” to format splice‑event files, then extract events for genes linked to the most significant SNPs (e.g., `grep –f ListGenes.txt splice3prime > Data_3prime`). The script also creates subject‑ID and splice‑event‑ID files.

steps.title: Run GTEx sQTL analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the R script “Analyze.R” to test association between SNP genotypes and splice events using linear regression with the same covariates as the eQTL analysis (pan‑cancer only).

steps.title: Summarize sQTL output
steps.instruction: Generate a table with chromosome, position, Ensembl ID, gene name, and splice‑event ID for each significant association.

steps.title: LiftOver GWAS SNPs to GRCh38
steps.instruction: Convert SNP coordinates from GRCh37 to GRCh38:

substeps.instruction: Import the GRanges object from step 11.
Load chain file “AH14150” via AnnotationHub.
Apply liftOver (rtracklayer) to obtain GRCh38 positions (script “GWAS.SNPs_liftOver.GRCh38_extended.r”).

steps.title: Extract GTEx eQTLs matching SNPs
steps.instruction: For each GTEx tissue, pull eQTL records whose chromosome and position match the lifted‑over GWAS SNPs (script “GTEx.eQTL.all.assoc_extract_GWAS.sugg.SNPs.server.r”).

substeps.instruction: Concatenate tissue‑specific files into one data frame, annotate with tissue source, and compute FDR per variant across all genes and tissues.
Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols/Entrez IDs (EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86).
Merge with the immune‑germline SNP annotation.
Retain variant‑gene pairs with FDR < 0.05 (exclude HLA and IL17R loci).
Optional: plot –log10(FDR) versus distance from TSS (scripts provided).

steps.title: Extract GTEx sQTLs matching SNPs
steps.instruction: For each GTEx tissue, pull sQTL records whose coordinates match the lifted‑over GWAS SNPs:

substeps.instruction: Run “run_split_sqtl.sh” to split each large GTEx sQTL file into smaller chunks.
Execute “r_extract.txt” with the GWAS variant object and each split sQTL file to obtain matching sQTLs.
Concatenate tissue‑specific sQTL results, annotate with tissue source, and filter to ±500 kb of the SNP (|tss_distance| ≤ 500,000).
Compute FDR per variant across all genes and tissues.
Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols/Entrez IDs (EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86).
Merge with the immune‑germline SNP annotation.
Retain variant‑gene pairs with FDR < 0.05 (exclude HLA and IL17R loci).
Optional: plot –log10(FDR) versus distance from TSS (scripts provided).

steps.title: Download germline VCF
steps.instruction: Obtain the TCGA germline VCF file from Huang et al. 2018 (see key resources table).

steps.title: Select samples with genotype and phenotype
steps.instruction: Create a sample list matching the “Sample List” used in Table S1 (Sayaman et al. 2021) and keep only those VCF entries.

steps.title: Prepare pathogenic variant list
steps.instruction: Extract the 853 curated pathogenic/likely‑pathogenic variants (Table S2, Huang et al. 2018) and write a space‑delimited file “list_snps.txt” with columns: chromosome, position, position, dummy variable.

steps.title: Split and normalize VCF per chromosome
steps.instruction: For each chromosome i, run:

substeps.instruction: bcftools view -r $i PCA.r1.TCGAbarcode.merge.tnSwapCorrected.10389.vcf.gz -O b -o CHR${i}.bcf.gz
bcftools norm -Ou -m -any CHR${i}.bcf.gz | bcftools norm -Ou -f human_g1k_v37.fasta | bcftools --missing-to-ref | bcftools annotate -Ob -x ID -I '+%CHROM:%POS:-:%ALT' -O z -o CHR${i}_norm.vcf.gz
bcftools +setGT CHR${i}_norm.vcf.gz -O z -o CHR${i}_norm_nomissing.vcf.gz -- -t . -n 0

steps.title: Convert normalized VCF to PLINK
steps.instruction: For each chromosome i, execute:

substeps.instruction: plink --vcf CHR${i}_norm_nomissing.vcf.gz --keep-allele-order --vcf-idspace-to _ --const-fid --allow-extra-chr 0 --split-x 2699520 154931044 no-fail --make-bed --out CHR${i}_norm_nomissing

steps.title: Recode pathogenic variants additively
steps.instruction: Extract the variants listed in list_snps.txt and recode them as additive genotypes:

substeps.instruction: plink --bfile CHR${i}_norm --extract range list_snps.txt --recode A --out OUT${i} --allow-no-sex

steps.title: Collapse mutations to gene events
steps.instruction: Treat a gene as a ‘gene event’ if any pathogenic or likely‑pathogenic variant is present in that gene.

steps.title: Collapse genes to pathway variables
steps.instruction: Group genes into mutually exclusive pathways according to the categories shown in Figure S7 (genotypic variables).

steps.title: Filter pathway variables
steps.instruction: Retain only genotypic variables that have at least 5 events across the cancer cohort.

steps.title: Gather phenotypes and covariates
steps.instruction: Download immune‑trait phenotypes (Table S2), genetic ancestry PCs 1‑7, sex, age, and cancer type (Table S1) for the selected samples.

steps.title: Annotate MSI status
steps.instruction: Add the MANTIS score for each sample (Bonneville et al. 2017) and classify samples as MSI‑H if MANTIS ≥ 0.4; otherwise MSI‑S.

steps.title: Run rare‑variant regression models
steps.instruction: Execute the R script “RareVariantAnalysis.R” to fit regression models:

substeps.instruction: Pan‑cancer analysis:

- For normally distributed phenotypes: linear regression of each genotypic variable (≥5 events) on the phenotype, adjusting for PCs 1‑7, sex, age, and cancer type. Apply log‑transformation to selected variables as indicated in Table S2.
- For skewed phenotypes: dichotomize into low/high and run logistic regression with the same covariates (excluding cancer type).
Per‑cancer analysis:
- Repeat the above linear or logistic models for each cancer type separately (omit cancer‑type covariate).

steps.title: Generate rare‑variant summary
steps.instruction: Create a master results file containing 9,138 samples, 832 pathogenic/likely‑pathogenic SNP/Indel events (586 distinct variants in 99 genes), and for each immune trait the regression beta coefficients and p‑values.
